card.name: Inside drug names, early pieces
card.fires_on: The first or second piece of a drug name split into parts, such as d in dextromethorphan, eth in promethazine, met in metronidazole, and d in contraindicated. It also appears at a few commas in opioid overdose text.

modes.label: Start of drug names
modes.description: The opening piece of a drug name that is split into several parts.
modes.example: over-the counter medications (e.g.,<< d>>extromethorphan), or herbal

modes.label: Inside contraindicated
modes.description: The d partway through the word contraindicated.
modes.example: Tramadol hydrochloride and acetaminophen tablets are also contrain<<d>>icated in patients with: Significant respiratory depression

modes.label: Opioid antagonist comma
modes.description: A comma in text about reversing opioid respiratory depression.
modes.example: If the response to an opioid antagonist is suboptimal or only brief in nature<<,>> administer additional antagonist as directed by the product

card.plain: It fires on the first small piece of a long drug name, as the model is still reading the name.
